$comment: SEED CORPUS — India. Read data/README.md before adding an entry. Two rules govern this file and nothing overrides them: (1) every statement is a real, publicly-reported, on-record remark by a public figure acting in a public role, carrying at least one live source link; (2) nothing here is paraphrased into the `quote` field — if the exact wording could not be established from a source, `quote` is null and `claim` carries a neutral summary instead. `stage` is the content-pipeline stage each entry has actually cleared (docs/03-content-pipeline.md §3.3). No entry in this file has cleared Stage 3; none is publishable as-is.

statements.neutral_title: On cloud cover and radar
statements.quote: The clouds could actually help our planes escape the radars and provide us much needed cover.
statements.quote_note: As rendered in English by the outlets cited. The remark was made in Hindi; the original-language wording is not yet transcribed. See `needs`.
statements.claim: That cloud cover would reduce the chance of Indian aircraft being detected by Pakistani radar during the Balakot operation.
statements.context: Modi described overruling expert hesitation on the night of the strike, calling the reasoning his 'raw wisdom'. The full interview is the context that must be captured before publication; the surrounding minutes are about the decision to proceed in poor weather.
statements.counterpoint: Radar operates at wavelengths that pass through cloud largely unattenuated; cloud affects visual and some electro-optical targeting, not radar detection.

needs: Tier A/B video of the News Nation interview with start/end timestamps
Hindi transcript of the exact sentence

statements.venue: Inauguration of Sir H. N. Reliance Foundation Hospital, Mumbai
statements.neutral_title: On Ganesha, Karna and the antiquity of surgery
statements.quote: It is said in the Mahabharata that Karna was not born from his mother's womb. This means in the times in which the epic was written genetic science was very much present. We all worship Lord Ganesha; for sure there must have been some plastic surgeon at that time, to fit an elephant's head on the body of a human being.
statements.claim: That reproductive genetics and plastic surgery were practised in ancient India, evidenced by episodes in the Mahabharata and by the iconography of Ganesha.
statements.context: Said to an audience of doctors and medical scientists while opening a hospital.
statements.policy_note: Borderline under Rule 1 (religion). Committee ruling: IN SCOPE. The claim under review is a claim about the history of medicine, made to doctors, in a hospital. The archive takes no position on the epics or on anyone's faith, and the entry must never be titled or captioned in a way that implies otherwise.

statements.office_at_time: Union Minister of State for Human Resource Development
statements.neutral_title: On whether evolution was witnessed
statements.quote: Nobody, including our ancestors, in written or oral, said they saw an ape turning into a man.
statements.claim: That the theory of evolution is scientifically wrong and should be removed from school and university curricula, because no eyewitness account exists of an ape becoming a man.
statements.context: Singh, a former Mumbai Police Commissioner, was then a junior minister for education. He repeated the position several times over the following weeks and challenged scientists to a debate.
statements.counterpoint: Over 2,000 scientists from Indian research institutions signed a joint statement rejecting the remarks. Singh's senior colleague Prakash Javadekar publicly asked him not to dilute science.

statements.neutral_title: On arithmetic and Einstein

statements.neutral_title: On escape velocity and social mobility
statements.quote: The escape velocity for earth is 11.2 km/sec while that of Jupiter is 60 km/sec. In India we have the concept of caste. There is an escape velocity here also. For a Dalit to achieve success the escape velocity required is that of Jupiter.
statements.claim: An extended analogy between planetary escape velocity and the difficulty of upward mobility for Dalits.
statements.context: The analogy was the substance of the speech, not an aside. It became a defining clip of Gandhi's early public speaking and is still cited more than a decade later.

This entry is indexed for the physics analogy, not for its subject matter, and the neutral title and any Committee commentary must stay on the analogy. If that line cannot be held in the copy, drop the entry.

statements.neutral_title: On the founders of Coca-Cola and McDonald's
statements.quote: Coca-Cola wala America mein shikanji bechta tha. McDonald's wala dhaba chalata tha.
statements.quote_note: As reported in Hindi by multiple outlets. The full-speech video and an exact timestamp are not yet attached; see `needs`.
statements.claim: That the founder of Coca-Cola had sold shikanji in America and the founder of McDonald's had run a dhaba, offered as an argument that entrepreneurial talent exists among those denied opportunity.
statements.context: Said while arguing that the government ignores skills and talent among backward classes. The rhetorical purpose is not in dispute; the historical claim is what is indexed.
statements.counterpoint: Coca-Cola was formulated in 1886 by John Pemberton, a pharmacist, and sold as a patent medicine at a pharmacy soda fountain. McDonald's was founded by Richard and Maurice McDonald, who ran a drive-in restaurant in California.
